intro: You're searching for a non-resident accountant near you because you have UK income or property interests but live abroad, and you need someone who understands the rules that apply to you. Whether it's rental income, a property sale or a UK tax return, a specialist can help you stay compliant and avoid surprises. iComply introduces you to a suitable UK accountant who can quote you directly for the work you need.
need_heading: What people searching for a non-resident accountant usually need
need_lead: If you live outside the UK but have UK income, you likely need help with the specific rules that apply to non-residents.
needs: You rent out a UK property and want to register for the Non-Resident Landlord Scheme so you can receive rent gross instead of having tax deducted at source.
You have sold or are selling a UK property and need to report the disposal and pay any tax due within the short deadline set by HMRC.
You need to file a UK self assessment tax return to declare UK rental income, dividends, or other UK-source income.
You are unsure how a tax treaty between the UK and your country of residence affects your UK tax position and want to claim treaty relief.
You have received a letter from HMRC about your UK tax affairs and need an accountant who understands the non-resident rules to respond on your behalf.
context_heading: What to understand about non-resident tax affairs
context: The UK tax system treats non-residents differently from residents, especially when it comes to property income and gains. The Non-Resident Landlord Scheme allows you to receive rent without UK tax being deducted, provided you register with HMRC. If you sell a UK property, you must report the disposal to HMRC within a short window, even if you have no tax to pay.

The word "accountant" is not a protected title in the UK, so anyone can call themselves an accountant. However, titles like Chartered Accountant, Chartered Certified Accountant and Chartered Management Accountant are protected, and members are bound by their professional body's rules on ethics, training and complaints. Every accountancy practice must also be supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, either by a professional body or by HMRC.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Where you live and whether you are tax resident there, as this affects your UK tax position and any treaty relief you might claim.
The type of UK income you have, such as rental income from property, dividends, or a pension, so the accountant can assess what returns are needed.
Whether you have already registered for the Non-Resident Landlord Scheme or need help doing so.
If you have sold or plan to sell a UK property, include the date of sale or expected sale and whether you have already reported it to HMRC.
Any correspondence you have received from HMRC, including deadlines or reference numbers, so the accountant can understand your situation quickly.
Whether you need help with ongoing compliance, such as annual tax returns, or a one-off piece of work like a property disposal report.
questions: Do you have experience helping non-residents with the Non-Resident Landlord Scheme?
How do you handle the reporting of UK property disposals for non-residents, and what are the deadlines?
Can you explain how the tax treaty between the UK and my country of residence might affect my UK tax?
Which professional body supervises your practice for anti-money-laundering purposes?
Do you hold professional indemnity insurance?
How do you communicate with clients who live abroad, and what is your process for handling deadlines?

faqs.q: Do I need to register for the Non-Resident Landlord Scheme?
faqs.a: If you are a non-resident landlord and want to receive rent without UK tax being deducted, you need to register with HMRC. Once registered, your letting agent or tenant can pay you rent gross. An accountant can help you with the application.

faqs.q: What is the deadline for reporting a UK property sale if I am non-resident?
faqs.a: You must report the disposal of UK property to HMRC within a short deadline after completion, even if you have no tax to pay. The exact deadline depends on the date of sale, so it is important to act quickly. An accountant can handle the report for you.

faqs.q: Can I claim treaty relief on my UK income?
faqs.a: The UK has tax treaties with many countries that may reduce or eliminate UK tax on certain types of income. Whether you can claim relief depends on your country of residence and the specific income. An accountant can advise you on how to claim any relief you are entitled to.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a Chartered Accountant and someone who just calls themselves an accountant?
faqs.a: In the UK, "accountant" is not a protected title, so anyone can use it. Titles like Chartered Accountant, Chartered Certified Accountant and Chartered Management Accountant are protected, meaning the person has met specific training and ethical standards set by a professional body. It is reasonable to ask which body supervises any accountant you consider.
